rationale: Total chromium is NOT a health standard for this matrix (Cr-VI is registered not-material: it does not persist and reference-method speciation does not detect it; total Cr is essentially all poorly-absorbed trivalent Cr for which EFSA 2014b set no intake value). This value is a PROCESS-CONTROL tripwire only: elevated total Cr is a documented signal of stainless-steel processing-equipment leaching (Hernandez 2019 attributes elevated total Cr in the French TDS to stainless-steel grinding/cooking equipment). 100 ppb is the 97th percentile of the non-soy total-Cr occurrence distribution rounded; a lot at or above it should trigger a manufacturing/equipment investigation, not an automatic certification failure. Precautionary tag.
evidence: fsa2016-infant-food-formula-metals-survey (n=51; single-source; P50 17 / P90 41 / P95 77 / P97 100 ppb)

rationale: Same process-control rationale as the non-soy row. Soy total-Cr data is thinner (n=10, P50 35 / P97 108) so the same 100 ppb category tripwire is applied provisionally rather than a soy-specific value; revisit when more soy Cr occurrence data is ingested.
